summary:
Product announcement from FMLink covering AHF Products' launch of Crossville Reunited, a porcelain tile collection intended for hospitality, corporate, retail, multifamily and residential interiors. The collection interprets marble and limestone with warm stone visuals and what Crossville calls refined movement, paired with the brand's FeatherSoft finish.

Three visuals are offered: Apuano, evoking warm Calacatta marble with a creamy white ground, light grey veining and soft tonal movement; Oro, with warm beige and gold veining on ivory for understated depth; and Avorio, a lightly veined limestone look in a creamy palette.

FeatherSoft is described as an advanced surface innovation developed through the manufacturing process rather than applied as a coating, producing a silky feel underhand and underfoot while retaining porcelain durability. The company says the finish still meets DCOF (Dynamic Coefficient of Friction) recommendations for most interior floor applications.

Specification details: glazed porcelain with rectified edges, 22 SKUs, multiple formats, coordinated mosaics and a full trim package. A new 6x24 format is positioned for vertical installations, fireplace surrounds and pool areas. An Avorio exterior version supports wet interior floors and exterior horizontal applications such as patios and pool decks. Product is made and stocked in the USA, which the company frames as supporting dependable availability and simplified project planning.

Terri Marion, Product Designer at Crossville, frames the launch as reflecting a shift toward spaces that feel more personal and connected to the natural world, suited to designers creating welcoming, restorative interiors.

Background: Crossville, an AHF Products brand founded in 1986, is described as a pioneer in the American tile industry and reportedly the first U.S. manufacturer of porcelain tile, with a portfolio spanning porcelain, ceramic, natural stone, glass, mosaics and specialty finishes.

No workplace policy, occupancy, or workplace-technology content appears in the item.
